steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease two 9x13-inch baking pans.

Beat white sugar, oil, and eggs together in a bowl until well combined; stir in flour, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt until batter is just combined. Fold in zucchini, 1 ½ cups coconut, and 1 ½ cups black walnuts until evenly distributed. Divide batter between the prepared pans.

Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into centers comes out clean, about 30 minutes. Cool in the pans for 10 minutes before removing from pans and transferring to wire racks to cool completely.

Beat cream cheese and butter together in a large bowl with an electric mixer until smooth; gradually beat in confectioners' sugar until frosting is light and fluffy. Fold in remaining 1 cup coconut, remaining ½ cup black walnuts, raisins, and vanilla extract.
Spread cream cheese frosting over cooled cakes.

raw_recipe.headline: Zucchini Coconut Cake
raw_recipe.description: This zucchini coconut cake recipe uses grated zucchini, which keeps the cake exceptionally moist, and black walnuts and raisins, which add texture.

review.reviewBody: First time using coconut— I’m a sucker for coconut anyway and in the black-walnut bread it’s WOW!

Both times I made it I used one 13x9 only. The first time I made it it came out great but it didn't rise much. I added 1 tsp of baking powder to the recipe the second time and it rose an appropriate amount to fill the pan as expected.

First of all, it is very tasty. I don't think I would call it cake but would call it bread. The picture shows two loaves with no frosting. There is a recipe for a very rich frosting. I did not make that. It calls for a 9x13 pan. I baked it in a 9" bread pan. It probably came up half way and did not rise any higher. I had to bake it 50 minutes. Something is missing somewhere because it would not make two 9x13 cakes. I made 1/2 the recipe. Even my husband liked it.

The second time I made it I added 1/2 tsp. baking powder to the whole recipe and it rose a little more. I also baked in six mini loaf pans 30-35 minutes. Easy to freeze and share.
I made this but cut it in 1/2 as I only needed one loaf and just spread butter on my slices. DELICIOUS!! I've already passed this recipe on.

Made it twice . Followed the recipe exactly. It didn't rise either time. I cut it in thirds , frosted it and it was very tasty. I really wish I knew why it didn't rise and I probably wont make it again because of it.

I have made this twice. Last time someone said it was the 'best zucchini bread he had ever tasted'. I am inclined to agree. The first time I made it with butter, and it was remarkably like the icing from a German Chocolate cake. Who doesnt love a cake that tastes like icing?! I do! I made it the second time with half pecans, half walnuts. I am just now starting on a third time.

I made this for Thanksgiving and everyone loved it!! Super easy to make :)
Thanks!!
